title: Annotatio II §.V open: Dissensus on Coena words/presence grows via Ubiquity controversy — Luther in dispute heat (Greater Confession)
pass_a_gloss: §. V. By which very thing the Dissensus of the Protestants, having begun in the interpretation of the Words of the Supper and in the mode of the Presence of Christ's Body in the use of the Holy Supper, took Increments, through the Controversy concerning the Ubiquity of Christ's Body, brought to that purpose by Luther indeed once and again in the heat of disputation, chiefly in two places of his Greater Confession, alleged by Calixtus, in the place cited, numbers 41 and 42.
pass_b_english: §. V. That same Protestant split — begun over how the Supper words are read and over the mode of Christ's bodily presence in the Holy Supper's use — then grew through the controversy on the ubiquity of Christ's body.
Luther himself, once and again in the heat of debate, had drawn it in, chiefly from two places in his Greater Confession — the ones Calixtus cites at loc. cit. nos. 41–42.
source_text:
§. V.
Quô ipsô Dissensus Protestantium, in interpretatione Verborum Coenae & in Praesentiae Corporis Christi modo, in usu Sacrae Coenae, exorsus, Incrementa cepit, per Controversiam de Ubiquitate Corporis Christi, à Luthero quidem in aestu disputationis semel atque iterum, duobus potissimum Confessionis suae majoris locis, Calixto allegatis, loc. cit. num. 41. 42.
